q: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III that is, they are in Groups ____ to 12 of the Periodic Table.
e: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III that is, they are in Groups 3 to 12 of the Periodic Table. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium ($^{21}Sc$) through ____ ($^{30}Zn$).
e: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium (21Sc) through zinc (30Zn). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium ($^{39}Y$) through ____ ($^{48}Cd$).
e: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium (39Y) through cadmium (48Cd). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum ($^{57}La$) through ____ ($^{80}Hg$).
e: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum (57La) through mercury (80Hg). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The transition elements are also called the ____ elements because the d orbitals are filled in these elements.
e: The transition elements are also called the d-block elements because the d orbitals are filled in these elements. D-block: transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first row of the transition elements is in the fourth row (Period ____) of the Periodic Table.
e: The first row of the transition elements is in the fourth row (Period 4) of the Periodic Table. 4: transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: In the 3d series, there are ____ transition elements, namely, scandium (Sc), titanium (Ti), vanadium (V), chromium(Cr), manganese(Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt(Co), nickel(Ni), copper (Cu), and zinc(Zn).
e: In the 3d series, there are 10 transition elements, namely, scandium (Sc), titanium (Ti), vanadium (V), chromium(Cr), manganese(Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt(Co), nickel(Ni), copper (Cu), and zinc(Zn). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: For the 3d series transition elements, the nuclear charge increases from scandium to copper so that atomic radii show a gradual ____ in their values.
e: For the 3d series transition elements, the nuclear charge increases from scandium to copper so that atomic radii show a gradual decrease in their values. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The decrease in atomic radii occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is stronger than the ____ force.
e: The decrease in atomic radii occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is stronger than the electron-electron repulsion force. Electron-electron repulsion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form ____.
e: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form alloys. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Although the 4s orbital is the outermost orbital, it is slightly ____ in energy than the 3d orbitals.
e: Although the 4s orbital is the outermost orbital, it is slightly lower in energy than the 3d orbitals. Aufbau fills lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy ones.

q: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys ____ rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added to any one of them.
e: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys Hund's rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added to any one of them. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: There are two exceptions to the expected regular filling pattern (half-filled or completely filled orbitals); chromium ($^{24}Cr$) and ____ ($^{29}Cu$).
e: There are two exceptions to the expected regular filling pattern (half-filled or completely filled orbitals); chromium (24Cr) and copper (29Cu). The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: In the case of $^{24}Cr$, one electron from the 4s shifts to the 3d orbitals to attain a more stable electronic configuration with the ____ 3d orbitals.
e: In the case of 24Cr, one electron from the 4s shifts to the 3d orbitals to attain a more stable electronic configuration with the half-filled 3d orbitals. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: The electronic configuration of $^{29}Cu$ is [Ar] $4s^1 3d^{10}$, instead of the expected [Ar] $4s^2 3d^9$, because completely filled 3d orbitals have extra ____.
e: The electronic configuration of 29Cu is [Ar] 4s13d10, instead of the expected [Ar] 4s23d9, because completely filled 3d orbitals have extra stability. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: When these metals form ions, the electrons are always removed first from the ____ orbital and then from the 3d orbitals.
e: When these metals form ions, the electrons are always removed first from the 4s orbital and then from the 3d orbitals. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: The electronic configuration of the iron(II) ion ($Fe^{2+}$) is [Ar] ____.
e: The electronic configuration of the iron(II) ion (Fe2+) is [Ar] 3d6. 3d6 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The zinc element has completely filled 3d orbitals and always loses the 2 outer electrons from 4s to give the electronic configuration of [Ar] ____.
e: The zinc element has completely filled 3d orbitals and always loses the 2 outer electrons from 4s to give the electronic configuration of [Ar] 3d10. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: Completely filled 3d orbitals are so stable that zinc can form compounds in the ____ oxidation state.
e: Completely filled 3d orbitals are so stable that zinc can form compounds in the +2 oxidation state. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: Copper is considered a transition element because the $Cu^{2+}$ ion has incomplete ____ orbitals.
e: Copper is considered a transition element because the Cu2+ ion has incomplete 3d orbitals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.
